::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 19th 1889  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54921: 171-2
:::

Dear [Mr Craik](people/person_379.qmd)

Here is <u>[the Reputed Changeling](cmy_books/cmybook_205.qmd)</u>. It really is a much better story than <u>[Beechcroft at Rockstone](cmy_books/cmybook_201.qmd)</u> which was chiefly written to run on with the [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) and satisfy people insatiable of continuations, so that as a young people’s tale it suffers from being treated as a novel.

Has it gone to [Tauchnitz](people/person_2124.qmd)?

What a curious book [Reuben Sachs](other_books/otherbook_1073.qmd) is! Is [Amy Levy](people/person_2381.qmd) a genuine Jew- ?[^1]

She seems to have stripped off all the illusions, not to say realities! about the race

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Amy Levy, *Reuben Sachs: A Sketch* (London, Macmillan 1888), a novel about upper middle-class Jewish life in London.
